problem: A well pumps a confined aquifer covered by a leaky aquitard. Water drawn down through the aquitard limits the drawdown, which approaches a steady cone.
result: Largest drawdown error: 0.410% of $C_Q$, over $10\le r\le30$ m and eight times through pumping and recovery. Leakage changes the drawdown by up to 53% of $C_Q$ from Theis.
scope: 3D quarter box, 0.625 m mesh, aquitard one element thick, 160 steps of 2 s; $\lambda=15$ m, vertical permeability 10 times horizontal. On meshes of 2.5, 1.25, 0.625 m the error falls with order 2.00. (a) radial profiles, with Theis dashed; (b) histories at two radii, Theis dashed; (c) mesh convergence.
meaning: This checks a layered aquifer system: an aquitard of a second material leaking from a fixed-pressure top, with the well, storage and radial diffusion of the Theis case. On the finest mesh the aquitard stores 0.03% of the aquifer's water, close to the no-storage assumption. Mechanical pressure feedback is disabled in this flow-isolation test.
